To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
knowledge is a complex and multi-faceted concept, and knowledge management is a process that is interlaced with the organizational strategy and processes.

Knowledge is the most important resource in today's knowledge economy, and knowledge management systems (or knowledge management technologies) are the tools that will help us manage this most important resource."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of information technology (IT) in the organizational process of knowledge management.
the development of an information systems architecture that can facilitate organizational knowledge management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the knowledge-based view of the firm is an approach that is based on an assumption that the most valuable resources of a firm is the knowledge and the knowledge management processes.
knowledge management is a strategic, systematic approach to achieving organizational objectives by managing knowledge as a first class resource.

knowledge management is an integrated effort to manage an organization's knowledge assets by creating, acquiring, sharing information, through training, and learning to create value from knowledge to support business processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
knowledge management and knowledge management systems (or knowledge-based systems) are the most important and most promising research areas in the field of information systems (IS).
we have provided a foundation for KMS research.
we have provided a foundation for the development and implementation of knowledge management systems (KM).
The main takeaway from our work is that

knowledge and knowledge management are important concepts in organizational theory and that they are closely linked with organizational learning, organizational memory and organizational intelligence.
knowledge and knowledge management are broad concepts and that they are being treated as significant organizational resources by both practitioners and academics.
the knowledge management process is a complex, multi-dimensional and dynamic process that involves the creation, acquisition, transfer, application and sharing of knowledge.
